snip.t: Drug susceptibility testing (DST): Determines resistance and guides the regimen.
Classification based on drug resistance according to Drug Susceptibility Testing
*Culture:* Gold standard for definitive diagnosis; identifies Mycobacterium tuberculosis and allows drug susceptibility testing
Culture allows phenotypic and genotypic drug susceptibility testing to detect MDR-TB or XDR-TB
Culture remains the gold standard, as it allows for identification of PCR-negative cases and drug susceptibility testing.

qs.q: What defines Multidrug-resistant Tuberculosis (MDR-TB) based on drug susceptibility testing?
o: Resistance to Rifampicin alone without agents
Resistance to both Isoniazid and Rifampicin
Resistance to any single first-line drug
qs.e: Multidrug resistance is specifically defined as resistance to both Isoniazid and Rifampicin, with or without resistance to other first-line drugs. Monoresistance involves only a single agent, while extensive drug resistance includes fluoroquinolones and injectables.

qs.q: A 45-year-old man with treatment-refractory pulmonary tuberculosis undergoes expanded drug susceptibility testing to guide management. Which specific resistance pattern is required to meet the criteria for extensive drug resistance?
o: Resistance limited strictly to high-dose rifampicin monotherapy
Resistance to isoniazid alone without any further resistance
Resistance to any fluoroquinolone and a second-line injectable
Resistance to pyrazinamide and ethambutol without isoniazid
qs.e: Extensive drug resistance requires multidrug resistance plus resistance to any fluoroquinolone and at least one second-line injectable agent. Monoresistance to isoniazid alone does not meet this advanced threshold.
